bibliography.abstract: Abstract The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a foundational driver of urban systems necessitates a structural evolution beyond conventional smart city paradigms. In this context, the objective of this paper is to examine how the Incheon Free Economic Zone (IFEZ), South Korea, can be conceptualized and structured as a district-scale AI city model that moves beyond connected smart cities toward AI cities. The study is guided by the assumption that this transition requires not only technological upgrading, but also the coordinated integration of urban AI architecture, governance mechanisms, service deployment, ecosystem formation, and phased implementation. To address this objective, the paper proposes and formalizes the IFEZ AI City Framework as a structured four-pillar architecture for smart-to-AI city transition. Building on IFEZ’s two-decade smart city legacy, the framework integrates an AI City Brain platform, district-specialized vertical AI industry clusters, a responsible AI governance layer aligned with South Korea’s AI Basic Act (2026), and a phased implementation roadmap for 2026–2030. The study further analyzes the institutional, infrastructural, and policy conditions that enable the framework’s implementation, highlighting how IFEZ’s institutional advantages—including regulatory flexibility, differentiated district specializations across Songdo, Yeongjong, and Cheongna, and existing high-performance computing infrastructure—support its role as a testbed for city-scale AI deployment and validation. Positioned within broader global AI city developments, the paper also provides a comparative perspective on smart-to-AI city transition strategies and extracts transferable design principles for urban policymakers and planners seeking to advance AI city strategies in their own contexts. The findings suggest that effective AI city transformation requires coordinated advancement in data infrastructure, governance, industry-specific AI applications, and startup ecosystem development, offering transferable insights for urban policymakers and planners worldwide. At the same time, the proposed framework remains conceptual in nature and requires further validation through expert consultation, stakeholder review, and implementation-based assessment.
bibliography.title: A strategic framework for transitioning from smart city to AI city in the Incheon free economic zone (IFEZ)

en.caveats: The proposed framework is currently conceptual and has not yet undergone expert consultation, stakeholder review, or empirical validation through actual deployment.
en.what: This study establishes the IFEZ AI City Framework, a four-pillar architecture designed to transition South Korea's Incheon Free Economic Zone from a traditional smart city to an AI-driven urban model. The framework integrates an AI City Brain platform, specialized vertical AI industry clusters across Songdo, Yeongjong, and Cheongna, a responsible governance layer aligned with the 2026 AI Basic Act, and a phased implementation roadmap spanning 2026 to 2030.
en.why: It provides a structured, district-scale blueprint and transferable design principles for urban planners looking to upgrade existing smart city infrastructure into coordinated, AI-driven urban operating systems.
